mainTopic: Whether flavorings like dill count as food, followed by a series of one-way rules in the משניות (priestly gifts, שביעית, kosher signs, ברכות)
overview: The amud begins with dill (שבת). It is obligated in פאה, so it is obligated in מעשר and gets טומאת אוכלין. That seems to show that anything used for flavor counts as food. The גמרא challenges this from a משנה about spices: רבי עקיבא says they are not impure as food, and in the final vote they are not treated as food at all. רב חסדא answers that dill is different because it is eaten in a dip (כמך). רב כהנא adds that ordinary dill is assumed to be for a dip, and he proves it from a משנה about תרומה dill. Next comes a series of משניות with one-way rules: every X is Y, but not every Y is X. They cover ראשית הגז and the מתנות, ביעור and שביעית, scales and fins, horns and hooves. The גמרא explains why roots need no ביעור, and why the תורה writes 'fins' when scales are the real sign. The last משנה says anything with a ברכה after has a ברכה before. The גמרא searches for an example of 'before only', and its final answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Dill is obligated in פאה, so it is obligated in מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that dill (שבת) is obligated in פאה, and therefore also in מעשר, based on the rule that whatever is obligated in פאה is obligated in מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But dill is obligated in פאה, so it is also obligated in מעשר. As we learned: anything obligated in פאה is obligated in מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins building a chain of reasoning about dill. This is the first link, and it sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know dill is obligated in פאה. A rule in the משנה ties פאה to מעשר: whatever needs פאה also needs מעשר. So dill must be obligated in מעשר too.

keyTerms.meaning: Dill, a plant used mainly to add flavor
The corner of the field left for the poor
Tithe, a tenth of the produce that must be separated

phrases.english: But dill, which is obligated in pe'ah,
is also obligated in tithe,
as we learned: anything that is obligated in pe'ah
is obligated in tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the chain of reasoning in this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dill, being obligated in פאה, is obligated in מעשר.

steps.title: So anything used for flavor becomes impure as food
steps.stepSummary: Because dill is obligated in מעשר, it becomes impure with טומאת אוכלין. This seems to show that anything used for flavor counts as food for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since it is obligated in מעשר, it becomes impure with טומאת אוכלין. Apparently, anything made for flavor becomes impure with טומאת אוכלין, since dill is used for flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the next link: whatever is obligated in מעשר gets food impurity. From dill, it draws a general rule that flavorings count as food for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dill is not eaten on its own. It is used to give taste to other food. Since it still gets טומאת אוכלין, the גמרא concludes that being used for taste is enough to count as food. This general rule is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The ritual impurity that applies to food
Apparently, so we see (introduces a conclusion drawn from what came before)

steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule ('flavorings count as food for טומאה') is exactly what the next source seems to contradict.

phrases.english: And since it is obligated in tithe,
it becomes impure with the impurity of food.
Apparently, anything that is made for flavor
becomes impure with the impurity of food,
since this dill is made for flavor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain from מעשר to טומאת אוכלין and draws a general rule
steps.raayaObject: The rule that anything used for flavor becomes impure as food
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dill case combined with the משנה rules linking פאה, מעשר and טומאת אוכלין

steps.title: Contradiction: רבי עקיבא says spices are not impure as food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a contradiction from a משנה: according to רבי עקיבא, spices like costus and pepper may be bought with כסף מעשר, yet they do not become impure with טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A contradiction was raised: Costus, amomum, chief spices, crowfoot root, asafoetida, peppers, and a cake of safflower may be bought with מעשר money, but they do not become impure with טומאת אוכלין. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule it just drew. Here are spices used only for flavor, and רבי עקיבא says they do NOT get food impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said that anything used for taste counts as food for טומאה. These spices are also used for taste, yet רבי עקיבא rules they are not impure as food, even though they count as food for buying with מעשר money. So the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (one source is set against another)
Second-tithe money, which may only be spent on food in ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא splits the two laws: the spices count as food for buying with מעשר money, but NOT for טומאה. Do not assume that being 'food' for one law makes it 'food' for every law.

phrases.english: And a contradiction was raised: costus, amomum,
chief spices, root of crowfoot,
asafoetida, peppers,
and a cake of safflower
may be bought with tithe money,
phrases.notes: This means second-tithe money, which has to be spent on food in ירושלים.

phrases.english: but they do not become impure with the impurity of food;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule drawn in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that anything used for flavor becomes impure as food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spices used for flavor do not get טומאת אוכלין according to רבי עקיבא, which contradicts the rule drawn from dill.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: the two laws should go together
steps.stepSummary: Inside the same משנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי objects to רבי עקיבא. If the spices can be bought with מעשר money, they should get food impurity. If they do not get food impurity, they should not be bought with מעשר money either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said to him: If they can be bought with מעשר money, why do they not become impure with טומאת אוכלין? And if they do not become impure, they too should not be bought with מעשר money!
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה continues with רבי יוחנן בן נורי arguing against רבי עקיבא's split ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that 'food' should mean the same thing for both laws. Either the spices are food and both rules apply, or they are not food and neither rule applies. His objection shows the tension between the two rules that the גמרא is working with.

keyTerms.meaning: They may be bought (here: they should not be bought)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא splits the laws: spices may be bought with מעשר money, but they get no טומאת אוכלין. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the two laws must go together. רבי עקיבא's ruling already clashes with the rule drawn from dill. The vote in the next step sharpens that clash.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said to him:
If they may be bought with tithe money,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין מִטַּמְּאִין טוּמְאַת אֳוכָלִין?
phrases.english: why do they not become impure with the impurity of food?
And if they do not become impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הֵם לֹא יִלָּקְחוּ בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר!
phrases.english: they too should not be bought with tithe money!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with a disputing opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that the spices may be bought with מעשר money but are not impure as food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being bought with מעשר money and getting food impurity both depend on the item being food, so they should go together.

steps.title: The final vote: spices are neither bought with מעשר money nor impure as food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי reports that the חכמים voted. Spices may not be bought with כסף מעשר and do not get טומאת אוכלין. This sharpens the contradiction with the earlier claim about dill.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: They counted the votes and concluded that spices may not be bought with מעשר money, and they do not become impure with food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with its final ruling. That ruling makes the problem with dill even sharper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the vote, רבי עקיבא held a split position: spices can be bought with מעשר money but do not get food impurity. The final vote says spices are not treated as food at all. So how could dill, which is a spice, get טומאת אוכלין as steps 1-2 said?

keyTerms.meaning: They counted the votes and decided. This is a formal vote of the חכמים.
Money that has taken on the holiness of מעשר שני. It may only be spent on food and drink in ירושלים.
The kind of impurity that only food can receive.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:
They counted and concluded
phrases.notes: The חכמים took a vote on this question, and this was the result.

phrases.english: that they may not be bought with tithe money,
phrases.notes: "They" means the spices from the משנה, like costus and pepper.

phrases.english: and they do not become impure with the impurity of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי: נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in steps 3-4 with the final ruling of the vote.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that dill gets טומאת אוכלין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The accepted ruling says spices are not food for מעשר or for טומאה. Dill is a spice, so it should not get food impurity either.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the teaching is about dill prepared for a spice dip
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the teaching about dill speaks of dill made for כמך, a spicy dip where the dill itself is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: When that teaching was taught, it was speaking about dill that is prepared for a spice dip.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction by limiting the dill teaching to one specific use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When dill goes into a dip, people actually eat it, so it counts as food. The vote in the משנה is about spices used only to flavor a dish. Those spices are not eaten themselves, so they are not food.

keyTerms.meaning: A spicy dip or relish. Spices ground into it are eaten directly.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
When that one was taught —
phrases.notes: "That one" is the teaching from the start of this discussion that dill gets food impurity.

phrases.english: it is about dill that is prepared for a spice dip.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: כִּי תַנְיָא הַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the teaching is about a specific use of dill.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dill is just a spice, so it should be like costus and pepper and not count as food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dill made for a dip is eaten as food, so it gets טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: רב כהנא: ordinary dill is also meant for a dip
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב כהנא refined רב חסדא's answer. It is not only dill specially set aside for כמך. Ordinary dill is assumed to be for כמך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said רב חסדא's teaching before רב כהנא, and he said: Do not say it is only dill specially prepared for a dip, which would mean that ordinary dill is meant for the pot. Rather, ordinary dill is prepared for a dip.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא adjusts רב חסדא's answer. He says the default use of dill is in a dip, not only when someone specifically plans it that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's wording might suggest that ordinary dill goes into cooking and is therefore not food. רב כהנא says the opposite: ordinary dill is presumed to be for a dip. So dill in general counts as food unless something shows otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say. It introduces a correction of a possible reading.
Ordinary or undesignated, with no special intention.
A cooking pot. Here it means cooking, where the spice only adds flavor.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said this teaching before Rav Kahana,
phrases.notes: "This teaching" is רב חסדא's answer from the last step.

phrases.english: (he said):
phrases.notes: Some versions have this word and some don't. The meaning is the same either way: רב כהנא responded.

phrases.english: do not say it is about dill prepared for a spice dip,
which would mean that ordinary dill is for the pot,
rather, ordinary dill is prepared for a spice dip,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּיה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines רב חסדא's answer by changing what counts as the default case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the answer: the default use of dill is for a dip.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only dill specially set aside for a dip is food. Ordinary dill is for the pot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ordinary dill is presumed to be for a dip, so it counts as food.
steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not arguing with רב חסדא's basic idea that dill in a dip is food. He only changes what we assume about ordinary dill.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה: dill that already flavored a pot loses its status
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings a משנה. Once תרומה dill has given its flavor in a pot, it is no longer treated as תרומה and does not get טומאת אוכלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Dill, once it has given flavor in a pot, no longer has the status of תרומה and does not become impure with food impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a משנה as the source for his claim. Here he is only quoting it; the next step explains how it proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After dill has been cooked and its flavor used up, it is just waste. It is no longer holy as תרומה and is no longer food. The key detail is the word "once": the משנה sets a time when the dill stops being food.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave its flavor into the food.
The portion of produce given to a כהן. It is holy, and a non-כהן may not eat it.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in עוקצין 3:4.

phrases.english: Dill, once it has given flavor in the pot —
it no longer has the status of teruma,
and it does not become impure with the impurity of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב כהנא's claim in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that ordinary dill is meant for a dip.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in עוקצין about dill after it has given flavor in a pot.

steps.title: The inference: before cooking, dill is food, so its ordinary use must be a dip
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה we learn that before the dill flavors a pot, it is תרומה and gets טומאת אוכלין. If ordinary dill were meant for the pot, it would not be food even before cooking. So ordinary dill must be for a dip.
steps.simpleTranslation: This means that before it gives flavor in the pot, it has the status of תרומה and becomes impure with food impurity. Now if you think ordinary dill is meant for the pot, then even before it was put in, its ordinary use would still be the pot, so it should not be food! Rather, must we not learn from this that ordinary dill is prepared for a dip?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא draws an inference from the משנה and uses it to prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dill's normal purpose were only to flavor a pot, then raw dill would be just a flavoring and not food, like the spices in the vote. Yet the משנה treats uncooked dill as food. That only makes sense if dill is normally eaten directly, in a dip.

keyTerms.meaning: If you were to think. It introduces a possibility that the גמרא will reject.
Rather, must we not learn from this? It introduces the proven conclusion.

phrases.aramaic: הָא, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נָתְנָה טַעַם בַּקְּדֵרָה —
phrases.english: This implies that before it gave flavor in the pot —
it has the status of teruma,
and it becomes impure with the impurity of food.
And if you think ordinary dill is for the pot —

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא נָתְנָה נָמֵי סְתָמָא לִקְדֵרָה!
phrases.english: then even when it was not yet put in, it is ordinarily for the pot!
phrases.notes: So the uncooked dill would just be a flavoring and not food, and it should not get food impurity.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this
that ordinary dill is prepared for a spice dip?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נָתְנָה טַעַם בַּקְּדֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 8 proves רב כהנא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: Ordinary dill is presumed to be for a dip.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied ruling of the משנה: uncooked dill gets טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: Conclusion: the proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: learn from it that ordinary dill is meant for a dip.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב כהנא's proof and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the contradiction. Spices used only to flavor a pot are not food. Dill is normally eaten in a dip, so it counts as food and gets טומאת אוכלין.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. The גמרא accepts the proof.

steps.whatToRemember: Spices used only for flavoring are not food. Dill is different, because it is normally eaten in a dip (כמך), so it counts as food for טומאת אוכלין.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Ordinary dill is presumed to be for a dip, so it is food and gets טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: First shearing and the priestly gifts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that every animal that owes ראשית הגז also owes the מתנות, but not every animal that owes the מתנות owes ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any animal that you must give the first shearing from also requires the gifts. And there are animals that require the gifts but do not require the first shearing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a one-way rule. Owing ראשית הגז always means you also owe the מתנות, but the reverse is not always true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראשית הגז applies only to sheep, because only sheep give real wool. The מתנות (foreleg, jaw and stomach) apply to all kosher farm animals, including cows and goats. So the sheep that owe ראשית הגז are a smaller group inside the larger group that owes the מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: The first wool shearing, which is given to a כהן
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, the jaw and the stomach

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this rule both ways. It only says ראשית הגז leads to מתנות. Cows and goats owe the מתנות but give no ראשית הגז.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Any animal obligated in the first shearing
phrases.notes: This means sheep. Their first wool clipping goes to a כהן (דברים 18:4).

phrases.english: is obligated in the gifts,
phrases.notes: The foreleg, jaw and stomach given to a כהן (דברים 18:3).

phrases.english: and there are animals obligated in the gifts
but not obligated in the first shearing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The dill discussion is finished. This is a new משנה with a new pair of rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראשית הגז always comes with מתנות, but מתנות can apply without ראשית הגז.

steps.title: Removal from the house and Seventh-Year holiness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a second one-way rule: all produce that needs ביעור has קדושת שביעית, but some produce has קדושת שביעית and needs no ביעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: All produce that has the duty of removal has Seventh-Year holiness. And there is produce that has Seventh-Year holiness but has no duty of removal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule with the same shape as the first. ביעור always comes with שביעית, but not the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every food that grows in שביעית is holy. That means you may not do business with it, and it is ownerless. ביעור is an extra duty: once a food runs out in the field, you must clear it out of your house. It applies only to food that actually runs out, so it covers a smaller group.

keyTerms.meaning: The Seventh Year, and the holiness of the produce that grows in it
Clearing Seventh-Year produce out of the house once it is gone from the field

phrases.english: All produce that has removal
phrases.notes: "Removal" means you must clear it out of your house once it runs out in the field.

phrases.english: has Seventh-Year holiness,
and there is produce that has Seventh-Year holiness
but has no removal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second rule in the same 'every X is Y, but not every Y is X' style.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביעור always comes with קדושת שביעית, but קדושת שביעית can apply without ביעור.

steps.title: Examples: the leaves versus the roots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives examples. The leaves of the לוף שוטה and the דנדנה have both ביעור and שביעית. Their roots have שביעית only.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: For example, the leaf of the wild לוף and the דנדנה have both. There is produce with Seventh-Year holiness but no removal: the root of the wild לוף and the root of the דנדנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second rule of the משנה with real plants. It shows both sides of the rule using different parts of the same plants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leaves of these plants dry up and disappear from the field at a certain season, so they need ביעור. The roots stay in the ground the whole time. They still have קדושת שביעית, but they never need ביעור. The next step explains why that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Wild לוף, a plant whose leaves and root can be eaten
A wild plant with edible leaves

phrases.english: GEMARA: For example, the leaf of the wild arum
phrases.notes: The גמרא skips a few words here. These leaves are the case that has both removal and Seventh-Year holiness.

phrases.english: and the ceterach;

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁבִיעִית וְאֵין לוֹ בִּיעוּר,
phrases.english: there is produce with Seventh-Year holiness but no removal:
the root of the wild arum and the root of the ceterach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains the משנה's rule about ביעור and שביעית with concrete examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leaves of the לוף שוטה and the דנדנה need ביעור. Their roots have קדושת שביעית but need no ביעור.

steps.title: Why the roots need no removal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק that is the source of ביעור. You may keep food in your house only while wild animals can still find it in the field. The roots never run out in the field, so there is no ביעור for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And for your cattle and for the wild animals in your land, all its produce shall be for eating." As long as the wild animal eats from the field, you may feed your animal at home. Once it is gone for the wild animal in the field, clear it out from your animal at home. And these roots never run out for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from a פסוק why the roots have no ביעור. ביעור is tied to the food running out in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links your animal at home to the wild animal in the field. From this we learn that ביעור starts only when the food is gone from the field. Roots stay in the ground and are always there for wild animals, so that moment never comes. They stay holy with שביעית but never need ביעור.

keyTerms.meaning: A farm animal kept at home

steps.whatToRemember: ביעור depends on the food running out in the field. Anything that stays in the field, like roots in the ground, has קדושת שביעית but no ביעור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical test for ביעור: does this kind of food still exist in the field for wild animals?

phrases.english: As it is written: "And for your cattle and for the beasts that are in your land
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:7

phrases.english: shall all its produce be for eating,"

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁחַיָּה אוֹכֶלֶת מִן הַשָּׂדֶה —
phrases.english: as long as the wild animal eats from the field,
you may feed your animal in the house;
once it is gone for the wild animal from the field,
clear it away from your animal in the house.
And these never run out for them.
phrases.notes: "These" are the roots, which are always in the ground for the wild animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the reason from the פסוק for the leaves-versus-roots split in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The roots of the לוף שוטה and the דנדנה have no ביעור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:7, which teaches that ביעור starts only once the food runs out for wild animals in the field.

steps.title: Scales always come with fins, horns always come with hooves
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives two more one-way rules: any fish with קשקשת has סנפיר, and any animal with קרנים has טלפים, but not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any fish that has scales also has fins, but some fish have fins and no scales. Any animal that has horns also has hooves, but some animals have hooves and no horns.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives two more one-way rules, like the rules about ראשית הגז and שביעית we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a fish has scales, you know it has fins. Fins alone do not tell you it has scales. The same goes for animals: horns tell you there are hooves, but hooves do not tell you there are horns.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (here written short as מַתְנִי')

phrases.english: MISHNA: Any fish that has scales
has fins,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְאֵין לוֹ קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת.
phrases.english: and there are fish that have fins but do not have scales.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קַרְנַיִם — יֵשׁ לוֹ טְלָפַיִם,
phrases.english: Any animal that has horns has hooves,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ טְלָפַיִם וְאֵין לוֹ קַרְנַיִם.
phrases.english: and there are animals that have hooves but do not have horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת יֵשׁ לוֹ סְנַפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the run of one-way 'every X is Y, but not every Y is X' rules from the משנה in steps 11 to 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scales mean there are fins, and horns mean there are hooves, but not the reverse.

steps.title: Which fish are kosher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a fish with קשקשת is a דג טהור, and a fish with only סנפיר is a דג טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any fish that has scales is a kosher fish. A fish that has fins but no scales is a non-kosher fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the משנה's fish rule means for כשרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since scales always come with fins, a fish with scales has both signs and is kosher. A fish with fins but no scales has only one sign, so it is not kosher. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ' כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת — דָּג טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: GEMARA: Any fish that has scales is a kosher fish;

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְאֵין לוֹ קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת — דָּג טָמֵא.
phrases.english: there are fish that have fins but no scales: that is a non-kosher fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת דָּג טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the fish rule of the משנה means in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scales alone show a fish is kosher; fins alone do not.

steps.title: Why does the תורה need to write fins?
steps.stepSummary: If we only rely on קשקשת, why did the תורה write סנפיר at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we rely only on scales, why do I need the word 'fins' that the תורה wrote?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the פסוק: if scales are enough, the word 'fins' seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every fish with scales already has fins. So in practice we only check for scales. Writing 'fins' in the תורה seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: Since we rely on the scales,
why do I need 'fins' that the Merciful One wrote?
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק in ויקרא 11:9, which lists both fins and scales as signs of a kosher fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule just stated to question a word in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word סנפיר in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Scales always come with fins, so the sign of fins seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Without 'fins' we would think scales means fins
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה wrote only קשקשת, we might think the word means fins, and then even a דג טמא would be allowed. So the תורה wrote both words.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had not written 'fins', I would say: what does the word 'קשקשת' mean? Fins. Then even a non-kosher fish would be allowed. So the תורה wrote 'fins and scales'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'fins' is there to make clear what קשקשת means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By itself, the word קשקשת could be misread as 'fins'. Then any fish with fins would be kosher, even one with no scales. Writing both words shows that קשקשת is something different from fins.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'fins' is not there to add a second test. In practice we still check only scales. The word is there so we read קשקשת the right way.

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had not written 'fins',
I would have said: what is the 'scales' that is written?
Fins, and so even a non-kosher fish would be allowed.
So the Merciful One wrote 'fins and scales'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא סְנַפִּיר הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word blocks a wrong reading of another word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קשקשת might mean fins, so any finned fish, even a דג טמא, would be kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה writes both words, so קשקשת must be something other than fins.

steps.title: How do we know which word means scales?
steps.stepSummary: Now that both words are written, how do we know that קשקשת is the 'covering' (scales) and not the fins?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the תורה wrote 'fins and קשקשת', how do we know that קשקשת is a covering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up: the two words are different, but how do we know which one is the scales?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing two words shows they mean two things. But maybe it is the other way around, and קשקשת means fins and סנפיר means scales. The גמרא wants a source that קשקשת is the covering.

phrases.english: And now that the Merciful One wrote 'fins and קשקשת',
from where do we know that קשקשת is a covering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקֶשֶׂת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 18 and asks which word is which.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that קשקשת means scales, a covering, and not fins.

steps.title: גָּלְיָת's armor proves קשקשת is a covering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about גָּלְיָת says he wore 'שריון קשקשים', armor of scales, as clothing. So קשקשת is a covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he was dressed in a coat of scale armor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק that uses the word קשקשים for a piece of clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גָּלְיָת's armor was made of plates that cover the body, and the פסוק calls it קשקשים and 'clothing'. So קשקשת means something that covers, which is the fish's scales, not its fins.
steps.whatToRemember: A fish with scales always has fins, so in practice we check only scales. The תורה still writes 'fins' to show that קשקשת is something else, and גָּלְיָת's armor proves that קשקשת is a body covering, the scales.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And he was dressed in a coat of scale armor.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 17:5, describing גָּלְיָת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק calls armor plates קשקשים worn as clothing, so קשקשת means a body covering, the scales.

steps.title: Then why write fins at all?
steps.stepSummary: Since קשקשת clearly means scales, the תורה could have written only קשקשת and left out סנפיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה write only 'scales,' and there would be no need for 'fins'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back its earlier question. Now that we proved קשקשת means scales, the word סנפיר still seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the גמרא said סנפיר was needed so we would not think קשקשת means fins. But the פסוק about גָּלְיָת in step 20 proves that קשקשת means scales, so that confusion could never happen. That makes סנפיר seem unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.english: So let the Merciful One write 'scales'
and there is no need for 'fins'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof in step 20 removes the reason given in step 18, so the question from step 17 comes back.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word סנפיר in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once קשקשת is proven to mean scales, nobody could mistake it for fins, so סנפיר adds nothing.

steps.title: To make the תורה great and glorious
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, together with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל, explains that the תורה gives extra detail to make the תורה great.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: 'to make the תורה great and glorious.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers that סנפיר is written even though it is not strictly needed. Giving full detail is part of the תורה's greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer agrees that סנפיר does not teach a new law. Its purpose is to add honor and fullness to the תורה. A word that seems extra can still have a purpose without changing the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He will make the Torah great and glorious (ישעיהו 42:21)
The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: A fish with scales always has fins, so scales are the real sign. סנפיר is written only to make the תורה great and glorious.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said,
and so too the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'To make the Torah great and glorious.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 42:21

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees the word adds no law and gives it a different purpose: honoring the תורה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every word in the פסוק must teach a new הלכה, so סנפיר would be wasted.
steps.terutzMaskana: סנפיר is written to make the תורה great and glorious, not to teach a separate rule.

steps.title: New משנה: blessing after means blessing before
steps.stepSummary: Anything that needs a ברכה afterward also needs a ברכה beforehand. Some things need a ברכה only beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anything that requires a blessing after it requires a blessing before it. And there are things that require a blessing before them but not after them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a general rule about ברכות. If something gets a ברכה after, it surely gets one before. The reverse is not always true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts. First: a ברכה after always comes with a ברכה before. Second: some items get only a ברכה before. The משנה does not tell us which items belong in the second group, and that sets up the גמרא's question.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Anything that requires a blessing after it —
requires a blessing before it,
and there are things that require a blessing before them
but do not require a blessing after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה after always means a ברכה before. Some items get a ברכה only before.

steps.title: What does the second part include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the phrase 'some need a blessing only before' is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an example of something that gets a ברכה before but not after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks in general terms. The גמרא wants to know exactly which item it means.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to include?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What does it come to include?
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's second line: things that need a ברכה only before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה's second rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which item gets a ברכה before but not after

steps.title: It includes vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The example is ירק: you make a ברכה before eating vegetables but not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vegetables get a ברכה before eating. According to this answer, they get no ברכה afterward. That makes them a clear example of the משנה's second rule.

phrases.english: To include vegetables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.

steps.title: But רבי יצחק says vegetables get a blessing after
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק holds that you do make a ברכה after vegetables, so according to him, what does the משנה include?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יצחק, who makes a blessing on vegetables, what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי יצחק says vegetables do get a ברכה afterward, so they cannot be the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer from step 25 works only for someone who says vegetables get no ברכה after. For רבי יצחק, vegetables belong in the first group, so the גמרא needs a different example.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yitzchak,
who makes a blessing on vegetables,
phrases.notes: He means a ברכה after eating them.

phrases.english: what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 25's answer does not work for רבי יצחק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יצחק, vegetables get a ברכה after, so they do not fit 'before only.'

steps.title: It includes water
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יצחק, the example is water: a ברכה before drinking but not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new example that works for רבי יצחק: water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if vegetables get a ברכה afterward, water still gets only a ברכה before. So water fits the משנה's second rule.

phrases.english: To include water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26.

steps.title: But רב פפא says water gets a blessing after
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא holds that you make a ברכה after water too, so according to him, what does the משנה include?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב פפא, who makes a blessing on water, what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge comes back. For רב פפא, water gets a ברכה afterward, so water cannot be the example either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer depends on someone holding that the item gets no ברכה after. Since רב פפא says water does get one, the גמרא must look further.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Pappa,
who makes a blessing on water,
phrases.notes: Again, he means a ברכה after drinking.

phrases.english: what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 27's answer does not work for רב פפא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רב פפא, water gets a ברכה after, so it does not fit 'before only.'

steps.title: It includes מצוות
steps.stepSummary: According to רב פפא, the example is מצוות: a ברכה before doing a מצוה but not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves away from food. The example is מצוות, which get a ברכה only before they are done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say it is talking only about food. So it can include מצוות, such as ציצית or לולב. You make a ברכה before them, and there is no ברכה after.

phrases.english: To include מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28.

steps.title: But in ארץ ישראל they bless after removing תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The people of ארץ ישראל make a ברכה after taking off תפילין, so even מצוות get a ברכה after. What does the משנה include?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the people of the West, who say after removing their תפילין, 'Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to keep His laws,' what does it come to include? To include…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of מצוות. In ארץ ישראל, people made a ברכה after taking off תפילין. The גמרא then starts to give a new answer, which continues on the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מצוה like תפילין gets a ברכה afterward, then מצוות are not a clean 'before only' example for בני מערבא. The challenge follows the same pattern as before, and a new example will be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: People of the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: 'The West' here means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל, where the גמרא was written. It does not mean a western country.

phrases.english: And according to the people of the West,
who bless after they remove their tefillin:
'Who sanctified us with His commandments'
'and commanded us to keep His laws,'
what does it come to include?
To include…

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִבְנֵי מַעְרְבָא דִּמְבָרְכִי בָּתַר דְּסַלִּיקוּ תְּפִילַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 29's answer does not work for בני מערבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בני מערבא make a ברכה after taking off תפילין, so מצוות can get a ברכה after too.
